correctness.rationale: The analytic proof exhausts all three-edge cuts of the 12-vertex truncated-tetrahedral graph, excludes singleton cuts by opposite edge midpoints enclosing the centroid, characterizes the corner events by ratios of four original vertex heights, and integrates their exact trihedral normal cones using Girard. This proves the iff odds condition and the uniform Haar probability in every Euclidean tetrahedron with 0<t_i<1/2. The equal-depth regular specialization and quadratic Taylor coefficient were calculated explicitly. Finite independent checks: all 32 combinatorial 3-cuts, 14,279 exact-rational direction comparisons, 750,000 simulated orientations (150,000 per depth vector), and analytic-spherical specialization; simulations are corroboration, not a substitute for proof.

value.rationale: Independent truncation of the four vertices is a natural four-parameter family of truncated simplices; the original centroid is geometrically canonical. The theorem gives a complete exact triangular-section probability and affine-invariant existence boundary under unrestricted tetrahedron shape, with a counterintuitive dependence on only opposite three truncations for corner survival. The regular case has a sharp quarter-edge extinction and computed universal quadratic exponent; this is meaningful structural classification rather than an arbitrary tabulation or routine recomputation of standard solid angles.
